llm_evaluation.text:
### 🩺 Clinical Observation

The AI detected patterns consistent with a largely unremarkable chest X-ray in this educational run, while the questionnaire notes a mild cough for a few days without fever. This synthesis is for learning only—not a clinical diagnosis.

### 💡 Clinical Context & Management Strategy

**Latest Developments:** For incidental or low-suspicion chest imaging in patients with mild upper-respiratory symptoms, contemporary practice emphasizes correlating radiographic patterns with pretest probability, viral seasonality, and evolving guidance on when outpatient monitoring versus early microbiologic testing is considered in standard care pathways.

**Standard Strategy:** In general clinical practice, clinicians often begin with history and examination, compare current films to priors when available, and reserve further imaging (e.g., CT) or laboratory workup for persistent symptoms, abnormal vital signs, or discordance between symptoms and plain-film appearance—rather than relying on screening AI scores alone.

**Key Concerns & Limitations:** Standard risk framing may incorporate age, duration of cough, smoking exposure, and exertional breathing difficulty from the intake form; short symptom duration without fever may be reassuring in some contexts, yet AI cannot exclude all pathology. Professional interpretation of the official radiology report remains essential.
